task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		Your phone has been showing 'No Service' for the past few hours.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! I'm hoping you can help me out. My phone has been showing "No Service" for the past few hours now, and I can't make calls or use data. I'm not super tech-savvy, so I'd appreciate some guidance.

turns.thought:
I'm sorry to hear your phone has no service — I can definitely help you troubleshoot that. First, I'll need to pull up your account.

Could you please provide either:
- Your phone number, **or**
- Your full name and date of birth (for verification)?
turns.execution_output: User: Sure thing! My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

turns.thought: Thanks, John. Let me look up your lines.

I've found your account, John. Let me check a few things on your line.

I can see your line (555-123-2002) is **Active** on our end, with no suspension and plenty of data left (8.7 GB of 15 GB used this cycle). So the issue is likely with the phone itself.

Let's start with a basic check — could you look at the very top of your phone screen (the status bar) and tell me what you see there?

If it's easier, I can walk you through checking it step by step.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me take a look at the status bar for you.

turns.thought:
Good — that tells us exactly what's going on. Airplane Mode disconnects **all** of your phone's wireless connections, including the cellular radio. That's why you're seeing "No Service" and can't make calls or use data.

The good news is your line is Active on our end and nothing is wrong with your account, so this should be a quick fix.

**Please turn Airplane Mode OFF now** — on your device, use the Airplane Mode toggle (`toggle_airplane_mode`) and set it to **OFF**. You'll find the Airplane Mode switch in your phone's quick settings/shortcuts panel (swipe down from the top of the screen) or in the Settings app.

Once you've done that:
1. Wait a few seconds — the phone needs a moment to reconnect to the network.
2. Look at the top of your screen again and tell me what you see. I'm looking for a **signal strength icon** (bars) to come back, which would confirm you have service again.

Go ahead and try that, and let me know what the status bar shows afterward.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, let me turn Airplane Mode off.

turns.thought:
Good — Airplane Mode is off, so we've ruled that out. I can still see two separate issues in your status bar:

1. **"No Signal"** — the phone isn't connecting to the cellular network.
2. **"Data Disabled"** — the mobile data switch is turned off.

Let's fix the easy one first.

**Please turn Mobile Data ON** on your device using the `toggle_data` control — set it to **ON**. (Same place you found Airplane Mode: in the quick settings panel or under Settings.)

Then, once that's done, please run a **network status check** on your device (`check_network_status`) and tell me exactly what it reports. I'm especially interested in:
- The **signal strength** (none / poor / fair / good / excellent)
- The **network type** it's connected to (5G, 4G, 2G, etc.)

That will tell me whether the "No Signal" is a network-connection problem or something with your SIM card. Go ahead and try those two things and let me know what you see.
turns.execution_output: User: I can only do one thing at a time on my end — should I go ahead and turn Mobile Data ON first, and then check the network status after that?

turns.thought:
Yes, that's exactly right — one at a time is perfect.

**Go ahead and turn Mobile Data ON first.** Once that's done and you've given it a few seconds, then run the network status check (`check_network_status`) and tell me what it reports for signal strength and network type.

Take your time — let me know when the data toggle is on.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, turning Mobile Data on now.

turns.thought:
You've found the root cause — this is a SIM security lock, and unfortunately it's not something I can resolve for you from here.

Here's the situation: your SIM card is locked with a **PIN code**. Until that PIN is entered on the phone, the SIM won't authenticate on the network, which is why you're seeing "No Signal" and "No Service" even though Airplane Mode is off, Mobile Data is enabled, and your line is perfectly Active on our end.

A quick safety note before you do anything else: **please don't start guessing the PIN repeatedly.** After a few incorrect attempts, the SIM will lock down even harder and require a **PUK code** to recover, which is a much bigger hassle. Since you don't remember setting a PIN, this needs to be handled by someone who can securely verify your identity and retrieve the right code for you.

Because this is a SIM security matter, I'm going to transfer you to our technical support team, who can assist you further with this.

turns.thought:
You're on the right track — that SIM lock is the root cause. Because your SIM is locked with a PIN, the phone can't register on the network at all, which is why you still see "No Signal" and "No Service" even with Airplane Mode off and Mobile Data on.

Per our support policy, SIM security issues like a locked PIN/PUK need to be handled by our specialized technical support team, so I'm going to transfer you to them now. They'll be able to help you recover or reset the SIM PIN and get you reconnected.
